title: Does the Action Matter? Probing Action-Conditioned Semantic Forecasting as a World Model for Autonomous Driving
abstract: arXiv:2611.24840v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: World models are increasingly used in autonomous driving to predict how a scene evolves under the ego vehicle's actions, supporting counterfactual reasoning and model-based planning. However, existing evaluations focus on prediction fidelity and planning performance, and rarely verify that the predictions depend on the conditioning action. In this paper, we study action dependence in action-conditioned semantic forecasting, which predicts future semantic segmentation from past segmentations and the ego action. We compare a forecaster with feature-wise and input-level action conditioning against an identical model without action input, and measure action dependence with test-time action interventions scored by standard segmentation metrics. The evaluation is validated in a synthetic environment with known action-dependent dynamics and applied to Cityscapes and BDD100K, both within each dataset and across the two vehicle platforms. Exper

translated_title: 动作是否重要？探究动作条件语义预测作为自动驾驶世界模型的作用
translated_abstract: 世界模型在自动驾驶领域被日益广泛地用于预测场景在自车动作下的演变，从而支持反事实推理和基于模型的规划。然而，现有评估主要集中于预测保真度和规划性能，很少验证预测结果是否确实依赖于所条件化的动作。本文研究了动作条件语义预测中的动作依赖性问题，该任务根据过去的语义分割图和自车动作来预测未来的语义分割。我们将具有特征级和输入级动作条件的预测器与没有动作输入的完全相同的模型进行对比，并通过测试时的动作干预（以标准语义分割指标评分）来衡量动作依赖性。该评估方法在具有已知动作依赖动态特性的合成环境中得到验证，并被应用于Cityscapes和BDD100K两个数据集，既在各自数据集内部进行评估，也在两个车辆平台之间进行跨数据集评估。
tldr: 本文提出通过测试时动作干预来量化评估动作条件语义预测模型的动作依赖性，以检验这类模型作为自动驾驶世界模型时是否真正依据动作进行预测。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes quantifying action dependence in action-conditioned semantic forecasting through test-time action interventions, verifying whether such models genuinely function as world models for autonomous driving.
